question: A 42-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 10-month history of joint pain and stiffness in her wrists and fingers. The symptoms are worse in the morning and improve with activity. Physical examination shows swelling and warmth over the MCP and wrist joints in both hands. An x-ray of the hands is shown. Synovial biopsy from an affected joint would most likely show which of the following?
analysis: The patient's symptoms and physical examination findings are suggestive of rheumatoid arthritis, characterized by joint pain and stiffness that is worse in the morning and improves with activity. The swelling and warmth over the MCP and wrist joints, along with the chronic nature of the symptoms, further support this diagnosis. In rheumatoid arthritis, synovial biopsy typically shows proliferation of granulation tissue, known as pannus formation, which is a hallmark of the disease.
